map_info.name: Melting Bernini: Noise as Sculptor
map_info.title: What keeps a body changing?
map_info.description: Three columns in one frame, the same mesh at the same resolution, the same material and the same mapped displacement range, differing only in what drives the melt: one held at a fixed phase, one on the shipped sine, and one on a real coherent field seeded by the room. Which is which is not written anywhere until a visitor presses REVEAL. The instrument logs both drivers and their displacement at the same moment; FREEZE stops time so the geometry can be inspected and repeated, SPIN turns a column without deforming it, MARBLE takes the veined shader off so material noise cannot be mistaken for the geometric driver. The columns carry no collider and hold nothing up. Corrected 2026-09-12: the previous description named an erosion process and an undoing of disorder that the shipped melt never implemented, the melt having been a sine with no field in it at all.

learning_objectives: Compare a held shaft, periodic deformation and coherent-field-driven deformation
Separate local time, whole-body rotation, material and vertex shape
Read a dark orb and its swarm variant as different recipients of earlier capabilities
Recognize bounded sampling and the limits of display geometry

map_info.name: Noise: What Does a Value Become?
map_info.title: Field, Reading, Combination
map_info.description: Three authored works: matching torus rings read a shared field as relief or colour; a compact basin retains the existing three-source terrain and exposes its weighted contributions; the dark orb keeps an independent pulse. FREEZE holds the current local moment, REMAP makes signed differences visible in colour, AMPLITUDE changes relief gain and FREQUENCY changes sampling coordinates. Terrain controls isolate resources before the original slope-lowering pass. Rings have no colliders; the terrain has a matching triangle collider.

learning_objectives: Separate a field from its receiving operation
Compare clipped and signed colour mappings
Distinguish displacement gain from coordinate scale
Inspect three retained terrain contributions and their combination
Distinguish shader relief from collision geometry

map_info.name: Voxel Noise: Discretizing the Continuum
map_info.title: Noise Carved into Blocks
map_info.description: A fixed Perlin field becomes a sampled occupancy decision. A cased 24-cubed model controls a five-times-larger volume with matching cells. A live screen compares one horizontal score slice with the exact occupied/empty mask; the dark orb keeps its independent pulse. Threshold changes classification, CELL selects a sample and screen layer, SEED changes the field, and CUT changes only the model view. Connected occupied cells do not establish a walkable route.

learning_objectives: Sampling continuous fields into discrete voxels
